game.title: Super Smash Bros. Ultimate
game.developer: Bandai Namco Studios and Sora Ltd.

core.fantasy: You are a toy-box hero in a bouncy party brawl, where the aim is to knock friends off the stage rather than knock them out.
pillars: Push off the edge, not drain a bar
core.signature_moment: Your friend is at a huge damage number, clinging to the ledge, and one well-timed swing sends them flying off with a star twinkle.

signatures.description: Hits raise a damage number; the bigger it is, the further you fly, and leaving the stage loses a life.
Danger shows on the fighter: smoke, flashing and a freeze-frame on a finishing hit.
Fighters from many art styles share one rim light, bloom and hit-spark language so they belong together.
Two attack buttons and a direction make every move; no long motion inputs.

audience.skill_floor: mash buttons and still have fun

period_s.method: Oracle reference study 2026-10-23: public knowledge (dev talks, reviews, store pages), in our own words; not yet measured on capture

rules.win: most knock-outs or last one standing

verb_count.method: Oracle reference study 2026-10-23: public knowledge (dev talks, reviews, store pages), in our own words; not yet measured on capture

rendering.signature: Every fighter keeps their own home look; one strong rim light, bright bloom and a shared hit-spark style make them belong to one game.
rendering.lesson: Mixed styles can live together if light, rim and effects are shared. Useful for Abbie's World characters made by different factories.

art.motion: keyframe; Hand-keyed moves for every fighter, tuned frame by frame for timing

body.note: One damage number per player along the bottom; the fighter smokes and flashes when high.

threat.note: Charge glows, items in hands and the stage edge show danger.

social.note: Player tags float over each fighter in big matches.

hud_coverage.method: Oracle reference study 2026-10-23: public knowledge (dev talks, reviews, store pages), in our own words; not yet measured on capture

screen_budget.fade_rule: Damage numbers stay; tags show when fighters overlap.

information_grammar.note: One number per player at the bottom of the screen; the bigger it is the further you fly. Fighters flash and smoke when they are in danger, and a big hit freezes the screen for a moment.

tricks: Hand-keyed moves for every fighter, tuned frame by frame for timing
Hit-stop: the struck fighter shakes in place, horizontally on the ground and vertically in the air, fading out; the attacker keeps moving a little
Damage poses are blended in, and shake scales with camera distance
animation.lesson: Hit-stop is animation: freeze, shake the victim, keep the attacker alive, fade the shake.

sources.title: Nintendo Wire: Sakurai's "Eight Hit Stop Techniques" and other episodes

animation.source: oracle motion study 2026-10-23 (public talks, interviews and breakdowns; no game files)

style: shared rim light and hit sparks across styles
expression: its characters, all borrowed from other series

take.setting: Knock the other brute out of the ring instead of draining health: nobody gets hurt, they fly off and bounce back in.
Show danger on the brute: puffing, wobbling, glowing; at most one tiny number per player.
Unify models from different makers with one rim light and one effects style.
